turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes identically in any structure possessing inversion symmetry, so centrosymmetric candidates can be discarded immediately (\(|d_{ij}|=0\)). Remaining candidates were therefore screened for the absence of an inversion center from the supplied lattice vectors and Wyckoff positions, leaving only the non-centrosymmetric tetrahedral families (zincblende, wurtzite, defect-chalcopyrite and related superstructures).

Within this set the magnitude of the largest independent component is controlled by three well-established structure–property factors:
- polarizability density of the anion (S versus Se versus Te),
- optical band gap (Miller’s \(\delta\) scaling),
- geometric alignment of the MX\(_4\) tetrahedra (perfect in zincblende/wurtzite, partially cancelled in many defect-chalcopyrite stackings).

These factors place the following five crystals nearest to the target value of 20 pm/V (typical DFT/experimental ranges in parentheses):

- 3C-SiC (zincblende, \(d_{14}\approx20\))
- ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) (I\(\bar{4}\) defect chalcopyrite, \(d_{36}\approx19{-}21\))
- \(\alpha\)-Ga\(_2\)S\(_3\) (aligned GaS\(_4\) tetrahedra, largest \(d_{ij}\approx19{-}21\))
- BeSe (zincblende, \(d_{14}\approx18{-}22\))
- 2H-SiC (wurtzite, \(d_{33}\approx16{-}18\))

All other non-centrosymmetric entries lie farther away: heavy-anion (Te,I) or small-gap phosphides/arsenides exceed 40 pm/V, while wide-gap oxides, chlorides and poorly aligned sulfides fall below 10 pm/V.

Final: c027, c050, c076, c037, c025
